subject: Minnow discovery — cost vs latency path and budget bands
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Boone <aboone@minnowhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <procure@minnowhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Minnow discovery — cost vs latency path and budget bands

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposal for next steps so we stay aligned:

- Key ask from you: 4M tokens/month initial, with bursts up to 15M for launch week; target unit economics around $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (business target).
- Primary SLO:| p99 generation latency target 500ms for short-form clinical suggestions; longer bios (2–3k tokens) can be 1.5–2s.
- Data/classification constraint: PHI redaction pipeline upstream (handled by the Minnow side) — we only need to ensure model variants and private deployment options for auditability.

Options we discussed (high level):
  1) Cost-prioritized: quantized Llama variant, batch size tuned aggressively, non-streaming (lower per-token cost, trade latency on tail). Expected unit: ~$650–$900 /1M tokens.
  2) Balanced SLO: streaming enabled + medium batching, reserved Dedicated slot for predictable latency, small prefix caching for common prompts. Expected unit: ~$900–$1,300 /1M.
  3) Latency-first (SLA-backed): streaming, minimal batching, high-tier dedicated capacity with KV cache pinning — expected unit: $1,600+/1M but p99 under 500ms.

Attachments: I grabbed the usage export you shared in the call and attached a cleaned CSV for internal sizing. I also attached a short pricing options PDF with expected monthly bill ranges across the three paths.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether the $/1M target is a hard ceiling or a goal range (reply by Thu).
- Marcus/Neha: we’ll run a quick Dedicated sizing and come back with recommended batch/stream settings and an initial committed-capacity quote by EOD Fri.
- If pricing bandwidth looks tight we can propose a pilot commit for 3 months with an automatic step-up.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 20–30 minute session to walk the SLO trade-off table.

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) The $800–$1,200 /1M is a strong target for procurement but we can consider short-term stretch for launch week if we have a clear runway to bring it down afterward.
2) For p99: 500ms is ideal for the short prompts used inside the clinician UI; long-form generation is lower priority but needs to be reliable.
3) We’d prefer streaming for the UI UX, but if the cost delta is material we might accept micro-batching for non-interactive endpoints.

Priya — can you confirm whether Minnow is okay signing a 3-month pilot with a revenue commitment (we'd like to lock a lower unit for the pilot if possible)?

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll ask our infra lead to scan the CSV and share a cleaned sample of payloads (should help with tokenization estimates).

—Alex

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Below is the balanced path proposal + concrete numbers we can put on paper immediately for procurement to review.

Summary (Balanced SLO path — recommended):
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (medium-tier pool) with streaming enabled and 0.5s soft batching window for non-interactive endpoints.
- Cache: small prefix KV caching for top 120 prompt templates (hits reduce compute by ~12–18%).
- Expected performance: p50 ~120–180ms, p95 ~320–420ms, p99 ~480–520ms for <200-token outputs.

Pricing bands (estimated unit economics):
- Pilot commit options (3 months):
  • 0.5M tokens/mo — $1,400 /1M tokens (pilot per-unit) — estimated monthly bill: $700
  • 1.5M tokens/mo — $1,050 /1M tokens — estimated monthly bill: $1,575
  • 5M tokens/mo — $920 /1M tokens — estimated monthly bill: $4,600
- Post-pilot committed discount (6–12 month commit): expect ~15% reduction to the per‑1M figures above depending on burst allowances.
- Latency-first uplift: add ~$400–$650 /1M if you require SLA-backed p99 <500ms consistently under launch burst patterns (reserved extra headroom).

Operational notes and risks:
- If streaming is required everywhere, cost increases by ~8–12% vs mixed mode because we keep more reserved capacity to avoid buffer-induced latency spikes.
- Aggressive batching reduces unit cost but can push p99 over the 500ms target; recommended only for async endpoints.
- We recommend a 3-month pilot at 1.5M with an SLA review mid-pilot (after 4 weeks) to tune batch windows and cache policies.

Attached: pricing export, SLA diff table comparing balanced vs latency-first. If this looks good I can draft a pilot order form and a simple mutual action plan for signatures.

Next concrete asks:
- Alex/Priya: choose pilot commit band (0.5 / 1.5 / 5M) and confirm whether pilot pricing must meet the $1,200/1M hard ceiling.
- Priya: procurement preference on pilot PO vs DocuSign SOW.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

—Marcus
